chunks: Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr narrated from Abu Ayyub, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Basir who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'What is the meaning of the saying of Allah, the Almighty: (O you who believe, turn to Allah in sincere repentance)?' He said: 'It is the sin which he never repeats again.' I said: 'And who among us has not repeated [a sin]?' So he said: 'O Abu Muhammad, verily Allah loves from among His servants the one who is tested [by sin] and repents often.'
ai.seo_question: What does 'sincere repentance' mean in the Quran according to the Imams?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Kitab al-Zuhd*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) defines 'sincere repentance' (tawbah nusuh) not as the absence of future sin, but as a firm resolution never to return to the specific sin committed. This interpretation highlights the Shia understanding of human fallibility, emphasizing that Allah loves the 'tested repentant' (al-muftan al-tawwab) who, despite being prone to error, consistently turns back to God. This concept underscores the dynamic nature of spiritual growth, where persistent repentance is valued over perceived perfection.
